problem: Find the value of $f(x)=\frac{{3}^{⌈5x-2⌉}}{x}$ at $x=0.7.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
Suppose that $x$ is a real number. The least integer (or ceiling) function $⌈x⌉$ equals the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to $x:$ 

$$
⌈x⌉=n,\,\text{where}\,n-1<x\le n,\,n\in Z
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=0.7,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.7) & =\frac{{3}^{⌈5(0.7)-2⌉}}{0.7} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{⌈3.5-2⌉}}{0.7} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{⌈1.5⌉}}{0.7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the least integer function, we have

$$
⌈1.5⌉=2.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.7) & =\frac{{3}^{⌈1.5⌉}}{0.7} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{2}}{0.7} \\  & =\frac{9}{0.7} \\  & =12.857\,14… \\  & ≈12.86,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
